body:
Acceptance at the top of a long dependency chain repeatedly reloads upstream review records. The Blocked guard introduced in ADR-0021 ran outside a read scope, so a single decision accumulated quadratic review reads and building an Accepted chain accumulated cubic work.

Reuse `@read_scoped` around the existing guard. Its transaction, conditions, errors, and researcher Acceptance authority stay the same. The new regression accepts the top of 20- and 40-node chains and checks SQL/review-read growth through the public researcher decision path.

CI headroom, in later commits: `timeout-minutes` 45 → 60; the module-scoped `chain` fixture in `test_performance.py` goes from 200 to 100 nodes (a single pass still means at most `CHAIN` visits, and a walk per node is about n²/2); pytest runs with `--durations=25`.

Validation: Standards and Spec audits found no issues. Independently reproduced the baseline regression (review reads 2166 -> 9126); the same test passes with the fix. At head `95bce91` all four CI matrices pass: Windows pytest took 33.1 min (3.11) and 43.6 min (3.12). The 25 slowest reported test phases account for 27.9% (3.11) and 26.1% (3.12) of total pytest time. Most runtime falls outside those phases; this measurement does not isolate its underlying cause. Windows timing is not addressed further here: macOS is the primary platform (#215). On macOS the core and studio suite passed at `95bce91`: 1143 passed, 26 skipped. No model trial was run.

Related: #211 exposes the inherited Windows CI timeout; this PR contains the separate performance fix and does not change #211. #213 tracks the remaining per-read SQLite connections.

T8 gap 2 (#197). After a Definition edit, the map's Warnings said a dependency had moved to a new accepted version, and nothing named the Definition.

`get_stale_cause(store, node_id)` follows `get_integrity_state`'s order and names the cause:
- `upstream-challenged` or `upstream-stale`, for an Accepted node;
- `support-withdrawn`, with the nodes the researcher sent back;
- `restated` (`node_id`) or `definition-edited` (`definition_id`), the newest change to the text the snapshot is read against, with `by`, `reason` and `at`.

`proof node show --json` carries it as `stale_cause`. proof-web's Warnings page reads it (zeqome/proof-web, fix/stale-cause).

Tests: three new cases in tests/test_unfixed_text.py; the contract, node, definitions, performance and attribution files: 157 passed, 2 skipped.

body:
Option C from the #132 tier 3 audit (A7). Every statement in the trial was unreadable. MAIN crammed the model's setting, its symbols and three conclusions into one sentence, and its four Claims began "In the setting of MAIN". Each proof then opened with its own "Conventions (reading of MAIN)", and the Verifier checked each against its author's reading. The design is ADR-0020 (`docs/adr/0020-definitions.md`).

## What a Definition is
- **The object:** a project's named piece of mathematical text (a definition, a model's setting, notation). It has an id, a term and Markdown text with `$…$`, is kept in SQLite (`definitions`), and has a CLI: `proof definition add|edit|remove|list|show`.
- **Naming:** a node names the definitions its statement is written in at creation, with `proof node create … --definition <id>`, and the names are fixed like the statement. A Split's children, a node created `--parent`, and a Claim crystallized under a parent name the parent's definitions too, plus their own (`--definition` with one `--child`).
- **Fixed once named:** a definition is editable and removable only while no node names it (`DEFINITION_IN_USE` names the nodes). A correction is a new definition, so no edit can change what an existing node says.
- **The interface:** the Accepted mathematical interface includes the definitions, by id. A node naming none keeps exactly its old fingerprint, so no pin or Acceptance moves.
- **Snapshots are unchanged:** they still freeze the proof, not the statement. Definitions are not in the manifest digest, so the verdict gate, the request-review gate and the Evidence bindings are untouched.
- **The document:** a new node's `proof.tex` opens with a `Definitions` section.
- **Readers:** `proof node show` prints the definitions before the statement, and `--json` adds `definition_details`.
- **Exchange:** a bundle carries the definitions. On import, a same-id definition with other text is refused (`DEFINITION_CONFLICT`), and a node naming one in neither the bundle nor here is refused (`DEFINITION_NOT_FOUND`).
- **Docs:** ADR-0020, the CONTEXT.md glossary (Definition, and the interface entry), the README, and the agents' skill.

## Tests
- `tests/test_definitions.py` covers the service rules, the inheritance, the fingerprint, the CLI and the exchange: 6 tests.
- Core plus latex-agent: 1040 passed. The 3 failures are the Tectonic and SyncTeX tests, which need the network the sandbox denies.

## Companions
- zeqome/proof-agents `feat/definitions`: every turn's briefing gives the definitions before the statement; the Decomposer writes Claims in them; every role may read `proof definition list|show`.
- zeqome/proof-web `feat/definitions`: the node page, the studio's node panel and the briefing hook show them; `GET /api/definitions`; the node form names them.

Each companion works with a proof-cli without this PR (it shows none).

body:
This takes prism-local, the upstream of `packages/latex-agent` (github.com/DengZhiyuan-math/Local-Ai-agent-for-latex), from the last take, `2938c05`, up to `37de720`. Upstream has 11 commits in that range. As ADR-0011 point 3 says, each is taken by hand, file by file, and the latex-agent README's "Taken from upstream since" records each take and what it left out.

## Taken
- **The context ring (d000c82).**
  - The Claude backend emits `{"t": "context", "used", "window"}` as each message comes in. The window is read from the result's `modelUsage` and remembered per model, so the next turn knows it from its first message.
  - `done` carries `context`.
  - A ring by Send shows how full the conversation is, with the numbers on hover. It turns orange at 75% and red at 90%, and New resets it.
- **"Show here" for the popped-out PDF (d000c82).** The top bar says the PDF is in its own tab, and "Show here" closes that tab and shows the PDF in the studio again. It is ported onto proof-cli's Web Lock viewer watch, because these files no longer match upstream.
- **The Claude Code profile folder (245a535), as a port.** Upstream sets it in its Home → Settings for the whole process. proof-cli's one page server serves several projects, so the setting belongs to each project:
  - **The setting:** `[studio] claude_config_dir` in proof.toml. zeqome/proof-agents#8 puts it into every turn's environment.
  - **Calls outside a turn:** the studio's account check, command list and usage probe now run with the turn's environment. This uses `Backend.env()`, which the agent manager sets from its context. They therefore see the login the turns use, and the account cache is keyed by the profile folder.
  - **Why it matters:** this answers #132 tier 1's first failure, where a server started without `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` gave every Start "Not logged in". The README now says how to set the folder.

## Left out
- **GitHub sync (d000c82):** files in the chat, `gitsync.py`, the History tab and the GitHub button. A proof-cli project's commits are the decisions recorded through `proof`, and an uploaded file would be an input outside the snapshot rules.
- **8b5f6c6:** gitsync's new-repository detection and the Diff panel's label.
- **Home and project management:** six commits covering Home folders, tags and grouping, project renaming, and per-project GitHub repositories. proof-cli has its own Home (ADR-0017).
- **d36e122:** upstream's README.
- **37de720, Deep Code as a provider:** proof-agents enforces a role's write scope and commands for Claude Code and Codex only, so a third CLI needs that enforcement first.

## Tests
- **New in latex-agent:** upstream's context test, plus a test that the account check runs with the context's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and is cached per profile. latex-agent gives 78 passed.
- **Sandbox-only failures:** the one failure is SyncTeX, because Tectonic needs the network. The core gives 958 passed, and its 2 failures are the Tectonic compiles.
- **proof-web:** its suite runs against this branch together with proof-agents#8. Only its port-binding tests fail in the sandbox, the same as on master.
